newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS TWO REV REPO TENDERS FOR TUES.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS TWO REV REPO TENDERS FOR TUES.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Tuesday said it had set two securities reverse repurchase tenders for 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), offering to sterilise an unspecified volume of market liquidity.
The NBS said in a statement that the operations would consist of a one-day reverse repo tender, as well as a three-day reverse repo tender.
The NBS added the American-style tenders would have no fixed minimum rate.

According to official NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector has a liquidity surplus, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 102.68 percent as of Monday, after being at 102.6 percent the previous day.

A week ago, Slovak interbank money market rates rose sharply due to a liquidity crunch, attracting some $150-200 million in foreign short-term capital, the bulk of which is currently deposited on the market.
The NBS holds tenders on a daily basis, if needed, instead of quoting securities repo and reverse repo rates.
However, the NBS said the move was rather meant to serve as a limited refinancing option, aimed at curbing the country's loan expansion by reducing refinancing volumes.
